rawFindings.title: Insecure HTML Extraction Leading to Unescaped Content in TOC
rawFindings.explanation: This change removes escaping of heading text in the table of contents helper by replacing `_.escape($(this).text())` with `$(this).html()`. Using `html()` directly inserts raw HTML from headings into the TOC output, which can lead to cross-site scripting (XSS) if the headings contain malicious HTML or scripts. Previously, escaping text ensured safe output by converting special characters to HTML entities.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore escaping for the heading text to prevent XSS. Replace line 29 with `var text = _.escape($(this).text());` after re-adding the lodash require statement at top of file.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: When rendering a markdown document with headings that contain HTML or JavaScript code, the TOC helper outputs that code unescaped as raw HTML, leading to potential XSS vulnerabilities in the generated HTML.
